blocks.text:
## What to expect in the Pantanal

Wildlife watching is at the centre of this trip. The programme includes a sunset boat ride, horseback riding, a 4x4 photo safari, kayaking and sport fishing for piranhas. Your lodge stay may also include trekking, birdwatching and a night outing to look for caimans.

Wildlife often comes close to the route. You may see capybaras and caimans by the water, along with herons, storks and kingfishers. With luck, you might spot a jaguar or a giant otter. Local guides lead each outing and explain how the animals behave and how this wetland ecosystem works.

On horseback, you follow narrow trails across open plains and marshy ground. The view changes on the water. You paddle along calm channels bordered by dense vegetation, while the boat ride on the Aquidauana River follows a bank of old riverside trees that shelter birds, mammals and reptiles.

The Pantanal offers photo opportunities throughout the day. In open areas, it is easier to see animals by the water. As sunset approaches, reflections and low light change the landscape. Your guides help you spot birds and other animals and explain how they behave in different parts of the wetlands.

Fishing is another way to get to know the area. You catch piranhas and release them back into the water. The fishing takes place during a boat outing, so the ride itself gives you another chance to see the riverbanks, aquatic plants and wildlife.
